# Postnatal CPI

Calculate the Combined Paternity Index (CPI) from mother, putative father and child calling outputs generated by [SNPcall](../SNPcall) or [DNPcall](https://github.com/fravasini/DNPcall).

## 1. Prepare the inputs

Place the three calling output tables in one directory and prepare the corresponding population-frequency table.

You can also provide a marker list to restrict the analysis to a panel. Input formats follow the [cfDNA CPI documentation](../CPI_from_cffDNA).

The examples provided here use:

- `MotherM1.txt`: mother.
- `FatherF1.txt`: putative father.
- `ChildC1.txt`: child.

R ≥ 4.2.0 and the packages `argparse`, `dplyr`, and `ggplot2` are required.

## 2. Choose the sites to analyse

Only sites with a homozygous mother are considered.

| `--site_selection` | Selection |
|---|---|
| `other_allele` | Includes sites where the child is heterozygous, so an allele different from the maternal allele is observed |
| `all` | Also includes sites where the child is homozygous for the same allele as the mother |
| `both` | Runs both selections; default |

The two selections appear in the outputs as `heterozygous_child_sites` and `all_compatible_sites`.

Sites with opposite mother-child homozygotes are excluded. A paternal mismatch is retained and contributes through the mismatch constant.

## 3. Set the minimum read support

`--min_child_reads` sets the minimum support for each called allele in the child. The default is `2`.

- A heterozygous child requires at least two reads for each allele.
- A homozygous child requires at least two reads for the called allele.

For a different threshold, use, for example:

```bash
--min_child_reads 5
```

## 4. Run the analysis

Download the repository and enter the module directory:

```bash
git clone https://github.com/lpistacchia/NEWPAT.git
cd NEWPAT/CPI_postnatal
```

### DNP example

```bash
Rscript Postnatal_CPI.R \
  --pileup_dir examples/inputs/DNP \
  --out_dir results_DNP \
  --trios M1:F1:C1 \
  --mother_prefix Mother \
  --father_prefix Father \
  --child_prefix Child \
  --markers examples/inputs/DNP/markers.txt \
  --popfreq examples/inputs/DNP/population_frequencies.txt \
  --site_selection both \
  --min_child_reads 2
```

### SNP example

```bash
Rscript Postnatal_CPI.R \
  --pileup_dir examples/inputs/SNP \
  --out_dir results_SNP \
  --trios M1:F1:C1 \
  --mother_prefix Mother \
  --father_prefix Father \
  --child_prefix Child \
  --markers examples/inputs/SNP/markers.txt \
  --popfreq examples/inputs/SNP/population_frequencies.txt \
  --site_selection both \
  --min_child_reads 2
```

In both examples, `--trios M1:F1:C1` identifies the samples in the order **mother:father:child**.

The filename prefixes complete those identifiers:

| Sample | Prefix + identifier | File read |
|---|---|---|
| Mother | `Mother` + `M1` | `MotherM1.txt` |
| Father | `Father` + `F1` | `FatherF1.txt` |
| Child | `Child` + `C1` | `ChildC1.txt` |

For files named `full_output_<sample_ID>.txt`, omit the three prefix options: `full_output_` is already the default.

To analyse multiple trios, separate them with commas:

```bash
--trios "M1:F1:C1,M2:F2:C2"
```

Omit `--markers` to consider all eligible sites in the calling outputs. Population frequencies are still required for sites contributing to the CPI.

Mismatch constants can be changed with `--err_const_snp` or `--err_const_dnp`, using the same options and defaults described in the [cfDNA CPI documentation](../CPI_from_cffDNA).

## 5. Read the results

| Output | Contents |
|---|---|
| `Summary_Postnatal_CPI.txt` | Tab-separated results for each trio and selected analysis |
| `plots/` | One PDF per trio and selection |
| `All_CPIplots.pdf` | All plots in one PDF |

Start with `Summary_Postnatal_CPI.txt`. It reports the number of sites, matching and mismatching sites, CPI, log₁₀(CPI), and the settings used.

With `--site_selection both`, each trio has two rows: one for `heterozygous_child_sites` and one for `all_compatible_sites`.

The plots show how log₁₀(CPI) changes as the minimum support for the obligatory paternal allele in the child increases. The red line and point mark the result at the configured minimum support. Matching and mismatching site counts are shown on the right axis.

Example results are available in `examples/outputs/`.

## NIPAT integration (0.8.50)

NIPAT exposes the scientific thresholds and mismatch constants through its scientific settings registry. The original scientific model is preserved; genotype thresholds are configurable, with the upstream defaults.

Each trio additionally exports `sites/<Trio>_sites.tsv`, including excluded sites and their `Status`, and `curves/<Trio>_<Analysis>_curve.tsv`. Curve rows represent exact constant intervals of integer read thresholds, from `Min_child_reads` through `Through_min_child_reads` inclusive. The curve increases support for the obligatory paternal allele after the initial per-called-allele support filter.

Samples shared across trios are read and validated once. Independent trios use the common bounded process budget; the coordinator writes ordered summaries and the aggregate PDF. `Log10_CPI` remains available when exponentiating it exceeds floating-point range.


### Run through NIPAT

```console
nipat --set cpin.min_child_reads=5 --set cpin.site_selection=both cpin --input-dir /data/calls --trios M1:F1:C1 --mother-prefix Mother --father-prefix Father --child-prefix Child --popfreq /data/population.tsv
```

`--panel /data/markers.tsv` optionally restricts the loci and requires REF/ALT
columns alongside SNP or DNP coordinates. SNP and DNP are analysed separately.
A trio is always mother:father:child; duplicate tuples, role collisions and
ambiguous filenames are rejected before staging. Shared parents may participate
in multiple trios in the same role. Native R retains the upstream filename
prefix `full_output_`; the NIPAT client defaults to `Mother`, `Father`, `Child`.
The R script in this bundle additionally requires the packaged settings,
parallelism and plot helpers; the engine supplies their paths.

All effective scientific settings and readable model constants are saved in
`work/effective-scientific-settings.json`. The source-pinned catalog documents
interfaces, formulas, data checks and output rules. The following settings may
be changed with `--set cpin.<name>=<value>` or a scientific configuration file:

| Setting | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `other_fraction_max` | `0.1` | Soglia della frazione di letture Other. Nei caller GT non assegnato quando la frazione raggiunge la soglia; nei moduli a valle sono ammessi valori fino alla soglia inclusa. |
| `homozygous_ref_min` | `0.9` | Frazione REF minima per classificare il sito come omozigote REF. |
| `homozygous_alt_max` | `0.1` | Frazione REF massima per classificare il sito come omozigote ALT. |
| `heterozygous_min` | `0.4` | Limite inferiore incluso della frazione REF per il genotipo eterozigote. |
| `heterozygous_max` | `0.6` | Limite superiore incluso della frazione REF per il genotipo eterozigote. |
| `err_const_snp` | `0.001` | Costante per un mismatch paterno su SNP. |
| `err_const_dnp` | `8.92303778101497e-05` | Costante per un mismatch paterno su DNP. |
| `log_cpi_lower` | `-4.0` | Guida grafica inferiore del log10(CPI); non modifica il calcolo. |
| `log_cpi_upper` | `4.0` | Guida grafica superiore del log10(CPI); non modifica il calcolo. |
| `min_child_reads` | `2` | Supporto minimo di ciascun allele chiamato nel figlio. |
| `site_selection` | `both` | Selezione dei siti postnatali; both produce due analisi distinte. |

The heterozygous transmission probability 0.5, homozygous transmission 1 and
mismatch indicator 0 are model invariants, available for inspection. Per-site
PI is the father's transmission probability divided by the population frequency
of the obligatory paternal allele; a paternal mismatch replaces transmission
by the marker-specific epsilon. Log10(CPI) is the sum of per-site log10(PI).
No eligible sites gives NA, not an artificial CPI of 1. Mother/child opposite
homozygotes are excluded; paternal mismatches remain eligible.

Plot dimensions, typography and output column names are presentation/format
rules, not scientific parameters. The two logCPI shaded-region boundaries are
configurable display guides and do not alter eligibility or CPI.
